one_line: A cited transfer-planning and Canvas counselor callable by an AI agent.
what_it_does: Combines official transfer-agreement checks with read-only Canvas course and deadline information, plus reminders and visible activity.
leverage_rationale: Structured deterministic queries over official agreements and private Canvas state, with citations and shared activity, make the agent materially more reliable than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: 13 page-registered WebMCP tools
Every answer cites an agreement row and year
Canvas token remains in browser and activity feed shows actions
execution_rationale: The packaging and described workflow are coherent and intentionally scoped, but no submitted video exists and the screenshot primarily shows a Devpost thumbnail rather than an end-to-end run.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows a dashboard with transfer target, courses, due work, and grade-risk panels
impact_rationale: It targets first-generation, working, and evening community-college students facing a concrete transfer-planning problem and connects authoritative requirements to their own coursework.
impact_evidence: Specific California community-college transfer use case
Official ASSIST/catalog sources and Canvas integration
Cited transfer audits and deadline/risk views
creativity_rationale: The combination of cited transfer agreements, personal learning state, and agent-visible actions is a fresh and ambitious education workflow.
creativity_evidence: Agent operates over both public agreements and private Canvas context
Deterministic engine rather than model-decided answers
usability_note: Clear student-oriented dashboard and citations; Canvas setup and breadth may add complexity.
red_flags: No video evidence submitted; execution claims are not end-to-end verified visually.
standouts: Strong evidence-grounding premise and useful combination of transfer plus Canvas state.
advance_reason: High-impact, agent-central education workflow with credible structured-state leverage.

one_line: A local-first outage planner where an agent simulates energy strategies for human review.
what_it_does: Inspects a household and outage, simulates and compares battery plans, explains unsafe intervals, stages proposals, and blocks stale commits.
leverage_rationale: Typed, deterministic simulation and revision-aware proposals give an agent reliable planning and safe shared state that generic UI driving would handle poorly.
leverage_evidence: Eight page-scoped tools
Structured JSON schemas and recoverable errors
Stale proposals rejected when forecast or workspace revision changes
execution_rationale: The described Morgan-household scenario, human approval boundary, and stale-state handling form a coherent complete demonstration; visual execution is only packaging evidence.
execution_evidence: Gallery includes proposal diff and stale-proposal states
impact_rationale: Households with batteries need understandable outage decisions under changing forecasts; the planner directly supports safety and autonomy without surrendering control.
impact_evidence: Concrete twelve-hour outage scenario with battery and reserve values
Unsafe interval explanation and feasible alternative
Human retains final control
creativity_rationale: The combination of outage simulation, explainability, proposal diffs, and stale-state rejection is a notably thoughtful agent interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent compares strategies rather than merely toggling appliance controls
usability_note: Evidence-first flow and visible proposal review should support cautious household decisions.
red_flags: No video submitted, so live agent invocation and result rendering are not directly verified.
standouts: Strong safety model: simulation, explanation, stale rejection, and human-only commit.
advance_reason: Excellent WebMCP leverage and unusually strong safety-aware planning workflow.

one_line: An attributed deliberation room for humans and AI agents to amend, support, object, and ratify proposals.
what_it_does: Runs civic discussions with explicit authorship, revisions, quorum, objections, deterministic ratification, and human-only closure.
leverage_rationale: Structured proposal state, attribution, amendment semantics, and deterministic quorum are difficult for a general agent to manipulate reliably through a forum UI.
leverage_evidence: Human and AI contributors are first-class and visibly attributed
Amend/support/object/ratify operations have explicit rules
AI cannot unilaterally ratify
execution_rationale: The product rules and civic-room model are coherent, but the packet has no video and limited visual proof of the full lifecycle.
impact_rationale: It addresses a real weakness in civic discourse: fragmented, reactive threads that obscure agreement and accountable dissent.
impact_evidence: Civic Housing Assembly seed room
Constructive objections require rationale
Consensus requires support to exceed objections
creativity_rationale: Consensus-first discussion with revisable attributed proposals and accountable AI participation is a memorable interaction model beyond conventional comment forums.
creativity_evidence: Explicit amendment rather than reply model
usability_note: Clear governance rules improve trust, though deliberation mechanics may feel heavier than ordinary forums.
red_flags: No video evidence; end-to-end agent participation is claimed rather than observed.
standouts: Strong civic interaction concept with explicit dissent and human closure.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-ambition social workflow with meaningful structured-agent leverage.

one_line: A browser-only CSV playground where an agent builds charts without seeing the underlying rows.
what_it_does: Infers a semantic model from a local CSV, exposes tools for chart construction and drill-down, and renders Vega-Lite visualizations locally.
leverage_rationale: The page can expose schema and render operations while keeping rows private, giving the agent useful structured context with a meaningful privacy boundary; a general agent could still drive much of the UI.
leverage_evidence: Agent receives semantic model, not rows
Seventeen tools reported
Charts, map, and California drill-down shown in gallery descriptions
execution_rationale: The simple no-build architecture and gallery progression suggest a working prototype, but no frame sheet or end-to-end video limits verification.
execution_evidence: Plain ES modules, Vega-Lite, and CSV parser described
Gallery states empty, loaded tools, chart, and drill-down
impact_rationale: It offers a practical lower-friction path for people who need quick exploratory charts but find Tableau or Excel burdensome, with local-data privacy.
impact_evidence: Explicit target of quick graph creation
Local rows never leave browser
Chart and geographic exploration workflow
creativity_rationale: The inversion where the page understands rows while the agent sees only a semantic model is a clever privacy-preserving interaction angle on dashboard creation.
usability_note: Promising simple workflow; chart breadth and canvas limitations are acknowledged next steps.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame sheets; only gallery/package evidence.
standouts: Privacy-preserving semantic-model boundary is a strong design choice.
advance_reason: Useful and well-framed data-viz prototype with a meaningful privacy/agent boundary.

one_line: A storefront an agent can search and operate through inventory and cart WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Lets a browser agent search a product catalog, apply natural-language constraints, and perform cart actions while showing the storefront.
leverage_rationale: Structured search and cart tools are convenient, but a competent general agent can comparably search products and click add-to-cart in this conventional storefront.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers on inventory search and cart actions
Built with usewebmcptool/WebMCP
Live Vercel demo reported
execution_rationale: The demo is reported alive and the concept is understandable, but the writeup is largely incomplete and no visual/video evidence demonstrates the workflow.
execution_evidence: Devpost text has empty inspiration/challenges/accomplishments sections
impact_rationale: Natural-language shopping can reduce search friction for ordinary shoppers, though the packet provides little evidence of a differentiated or deep commerce problem.
impact_evidence: Concrete skincare-under-$25 example
Search and cart are user-facing goals
Real-time inventory claim
creativity_rationale: An agent-operated catalog and cart is a familiar WebMCP commerce pattern with little demonstrated novelty beyond implementation.
creativity_evidence: No unusual interaction or domain constraint shown
usability_note: Natural-language search is approachable, but evidence is too thin to judge cart quality or edge cases.
advance_reason: Conventional concept with thin execution evidence and an incomplete submission narrative.

one_line: An evidence-bound resume and application workspace where agents propose but humans approve grounded edits.
what_it_does: Matches resumes to postings, checks claims against a personal fact bank, proposes cited diffs, gates cover letters and submission behind human review.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central to exposing a changing capability boundary, enforcing grounding constraints, sharing proposal state, and preventing unauthorized application actions; UI-driving agents could not reliably reproduce these guarantees.
leverage_evidence: 13 direct page tools with posting-dependent capability boundary
Ungrounded Kubernetes/TensorFlow claims rejected by page rule
Proposals are diffs requiring human approval; submit appears only after assembly and still requires confirmation
execution_rationale: The 150-second video transcript demonstrates the central workflow, including rejection, evidence citations, proposal approval, cover-letter gating, and capability changes; the package is coherent and unusually complete.
execution_evidence: Video transcript shows fit check, refusal of unsupported claims, grounded diffs, approval, and submission gate
120 real ML postings from three APIs
Video and five gallery images submitted
impact_rationale: It addresses a consequential and common job-application failure: fluent resumes silently inventing experience, while still helping applicants tailor materials efficiently.
impact_evidence: Evidence-bound fact bank from user's CV
Unsupported requirements explicitly surfaced rather than hidden
Human approval before application submission
creativity_rationale: The page—not the model—sets claim authority, and the tool registry itself changes with approval state. This is a memorable, deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Every proposed sentence carries quoted source facts
Cross-project combinations are flagged rather than falsely treated as proven
usability_note: Diff review and explicit evidence support trust, though the workflow is necessarily more deliberate than ordinary resume generation.
red_flags: No major red flag; transcript acknowledges cross-project combination limits.
standouts: Exceptional evidence-bound safety model and demonstrated human-agent capability boundary.
advance_reason: Top-tier WebMCP leverage, execution, impact, and creativity, supported by unusually direct video evidence.

one_line: A WebMCP-native project coordination workspace that diagnoses blockers and stages verified recovery plans.
what_it_does: Inspects dependency graphs, simulates schedule changes, respects negative constraints, and stages transparent mutations for human approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured live project state, dry-run feasibility checks, constraints, and staged writes give agents reliable operational control beyond generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Live workspace inspection and mathematical schedule simulation
Negative constraints such as not reassigning a named person
Zero-unchecked-mutation gate described
execution_rationale: The product scope and safeguards are coherent, but no transcript or video was submitted, so central execution remains claimed rather than directly observed.
execution_evidence: Detailed workflow and guardrails in about text
impact_rationale: Engineering managers and leads have a concrete need to diagnose launch blockers and safely evaluate schedule recovery under constraints.
impact_evidence: Specific critical-launch crisis scenario
Dependency cascades and slack buffers are actionable project state
Human-controlled staging rather than unchecked writes
creativity_rationale: Verified schedule recovery with negative-constraint reasoning is a strong synthesis, though project coordination itself is established.
creativity_evidence: Agent as verified operator rather than advice chatbot
usability_note: Staging and review should improve trust; workflow complexity may be high for teams without clean dependency data.
red_flags: No video evidence and no repository; execution claims are weakly verifiable.
standouts: Constraint-aware dry-run plus human mutation gate.
advance_reason: Strong operational use case and meaningful agent leverage despite thin execution evidence.

leverage_rationale: Searching rare-copy condition and note content through structured tools is more expressive and reliable than clicking a small catalog, though the basic reserve action remains UI-replicable.

Search includes condition and interior-note text
Agent/human actions share one logic and live activity panel
execution_rationale: The single-file implementation and described catalog/reservation lifecycle are plausible, but there is no video and only one gallery image, limiting end-to-end confidence.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo reported
Same functions used for human and agent flows
impact_rationale: It serves readers interested in browsing distinctive second-hand books and makes scarcity/reservation meaningful, though the inventory is fictional and intentionally small.
impact_evidence: Unique-copy scarcity is central to the shopping experience
Search by notes and condition
24-hour reservation

one_line: A hotel-booking retry proof that checks whether a lost-response booking already succeeded.
what_it_does: Exposes safe check/prepare/recover/cancellation-preview operations while keeping confirm, payment, and cancellation human-only.
leverage_rationale: The core value is an idempotency/status query over shared booking state that prevents duplicate reservations—precisely the kind of structured operation a UI-driving agent cannot safely infer after a lost response.
leverage_evidence: Four narrow WebMCP capabilities for check, prepare, recovery, and cancellation preview
Agent cannot confirm, pay, or cancel
Demonstrated two attempts but one simulated booking/effect/confirmation
execution_rationale: The scenario is tightly scoped and the claimed outcome is precise, but no video was submitted and the frame references appear unavailable as direct proof in this review.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo reported
impact_rationale: Duplicate bookings during unreliable connectivity are a real, high-stress travel and transaction problem; the intervention gives a clear answer without risky resubmission.
impact_evidence: Airport Wi-Fi lost-response scenario
One booking after two attempts
Generalizes to payments, reservations, and submissions
creativity_rationale: The project focuses on uncertainty and idempotent recovery rather than the usual shopping/booking automation, with a concise and memorable safety interaction.
creativity_evidence: Ask whether exact booking already went through
Safe status recovery without adding authority
usability_note: A single safe status question is easy to understand and reduces stressful retry decisions.
red_flags: No video evidence; fictional hotel scenario and simulated booking limit external validation.
standouts: Excellent narrow safety problem with strong WebMCP indispensability.
advance_reason: Highly defensible WebMCP leverage on a concrete transaction-safety problem.

one_line: An agent-directed studio that renders fictional coding-agent sessions as SVG, images, and video.
what_it_does: Lets agents author scripts, control camera/look/surface, preview timelines and frames, propose approved rewrites, and export deterministic media.
leverage_rationale: The agent can inspect timing and rendered frames—facts unavailable from text alone—and operate a shared stage through structured tools, making the collaboration substantially more reliable than copy/paste or UI driving.
leverage_evidence: 13 site tools
inspect_timeline and snapshot_frame expose rendered state
Every-word list, approval cards, and export confirmation preserve shared human-agent state
execution_rationale: The 170-second transcript walks through authoring, playback, choices, voice input, visual changes, terminal surface, and export; the coherent studio scope appears highly complete.
execution_evidence: Video transcript shows script load, camera, playback, choices, voice input, theme/backdrop, and export
Two showcase scripts and gallery images
impact_rationale: Documentation, README, talks, and social posts need repeatable session visuals without leaking secrets or relying on re-recording real agent sessions.
impact_evidence: Explicit use cases: READMEs, docs, talks, posts
Client-only/privacy default
Exports SVG, PNG, GIF, and MP4
creativity_rationale: A fictional-session stage that agents can directly author and inspect, with choices, timing, voice, and deterministic rendering, is a highly original creative tool concept.
creativity_evidence: Rendered-stage introspection by frame and timeline
Same script across app and terminal surfaces
usability_note: Approval cards, timeline review, and deterministic exports support controlled creative iteration.
red_flags: The output is a fictional reconstruction rather than a recording of a real session, so audience fit depends on wanting stylized demos.
standouts: Strong agent/stage shared-state model and unusually complete creative workflow.
advance_reason: Distinctive, well-demonstrated creative medium with strong agent-native inspection and authoring.
